dedupe_keys.name: bof pss2 payment and settlement system simulator

description: BoF-PSS2 is the Bank of Finland's simulator of interbank payment and securities settlement systems, completed in spring 2004 for external use and international distribution after an earlier internal simulator had proved useful for studying liquidity needs and system risks during Finland's entry to Economic and Monetary Union. The article by Leinonen (Bank of Finland) and Soramaki (European Central Bank) describes simulation as a laboratory for payment systems: it lets analysts replicate settlement processing with large volumes of transactions, embed different behaviour models of participants, compare structural options and decision parameters, and study crisis scenarios that are too risky to test on live systems. Detailed design is in Bank of Finland Discussion Paper 23/2003. The simulator was made available for research purposes free of charge; use has been global among central banks and researchers. Caveats: the simulator's former web page on suomenpankki.fi returned 404 on 26 September 2026, so current distribution, version and licence terms could not be confirmed, and simulations need confidential transaction data from system operators. For simulation it models liquidity flows, gridlock and participant failures in RTGS and settlement systems for resilience and cascading-failure studies of financial infrastructure. Related catalogue records include the Fedwire and RITS statistics and ABIDES.
